title: One rigid opacity map at 4.75 stellar radii per day fits three TESS dips of G4466 below the rectangular-screen speed limits
abstract: We test whether the TESS dips of the mature dusty dwarf G4466 require speeds above 7 stellar radii per day for all rigid screens. We reuse the published 10-minute light curve and allow a fixed map with cell opacity from zero to one. One map at 4.75 stellar radii per day fits all 357 measurements across three dips and the data between them. It has a constant unocculted flux of 1.06 in the source units and no baseline slope. Finer integration gives chi-square 237.18 with the source reference error of 0.0064 and residual RMS 0.005217. Separate fits predict alternating held-out measurements with RMS 0.00742 and 0.00670. Thus the stronger reported speed limits depend on screen geometry. The source crescent bound remains valid. At the tested speed, circular orbit examples are 2.20 times farther out than at 7.05 stellar radii per day. This is an existence test, not a speed estimate or evidence for these particular maps. Many cells, fine structure, an uncertain bare-star flux, fixed source calibration and correlated noise limit physical interpretation. We do not establish a new lower speed bound or dust at several au. We supply masks, code, licensed input photometry, attribution, provenance and reproduction instructions.
